question: Why does nums = nums.sort() lead to the error 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'append'?
answer: nums = nums.sort() leads to the error 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'append' because list.sort() sorts in place and returns None. [S1] To avoid this, use nums.sort() on its own line or use sorted(nums) to get a new sorted list [S1] [S7].

KeyError is raised when a dictionary key is missing. IndexError is raised when a sequence index is

S3.title: Python Lecture Notes
S3.text: 3. Functions A function is a reusable block of code defined with def. Parameters are the names in the definition; arguments are the values supplied in a call. A function returns a value with return; if no return statement runs, the function returns None. Default parameter values, as in def greet(name, greeting="Hello"), let callers omit an argument. Keyword arguments, as in greet(greeting="Hi", name="Sara"), make calls explicit. *args collects extra positional arguments into a tuple, and **kwargs collects extra keyword arguments into a dictionary. Never use a mutable object such as a list as a default value. The default is created once when the function is defined, so def add(x, bucket=[]) shares one list across all calls. The safe pattern is bucket=None followed by if bucket is None: bucket = []. Variables created inside a function are local to it.

NULL: the SQL marker for a missing value.

None: Python's null object; pandas also treats None as missing in object columns.
key: the column or columns used to match rows when joining two tables.
schema: the names and data types of the columns of a table.
sample: DataFrame.sample(n=3) returns 3 random rows. It is a row draw, not a statistical sample design.

BUILT-IN FUNCTIONS
len(x) returns the number of items in x.
sum(nums) adds the numbers in an iterable.
min(nums) and max(nums) return the smallest and largest items.
sorted(items) returns a new sorted list; list.sort() sorts in place and returns None.
enumerate(items) gives (index, item) pairs.
zip(a, b) pairs items from two iterables and stops at the shortest.
range(stop) generates 0 .. stop-1; range(start, stop, step) supports steps.
isinstance(x, int) tests whether x is an instance of a type.

S9.title: Python Reference Notes
S9.text:
COMMON ERRORS AND THEIR MEANING
SyntaxError: the code is not valid Python, for example a missing colon after if.
IndentationError: the indentation of a block is inconsistent.
NameError: a variable or function name was used before it was defined.
TypeError: an operation was applied to the wrong type, such as "a" + 1.
ValueError: the type is right but the value is not, such as int("abc").
KeyError: a dictionary key does not exist.
IndexError: a list index is outside the valid range.
ZeroDivisionError: division or modulo by zero.
FileNotFoundError: the file path does not exist.
